exposure: Intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) levels (antepartum, postpartum, and difference)
Hypertension in Pregnancy (HIP) status (normotensive vs. HIP)
outcome: Intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) levels (antepartum, postpartum, and difference)
cohort: The study included seventy pregnant women (55 normotensive, 15 with hypertension in pregnancy) undergoing antepartum, non-emergency caesarean delivery.
finding: Higher antepartum and postpartum intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) levels are associated with hypertension in pregnancy (HIP), and the reduction of IAP from antepartum to postpartum was less in the HIP group.
cross-section timing: Measurements were performed antepartum and immediately postpartum in women undergoing non-emergency caesarean delivery.
gest_age: The mean gestational age for normotensive pregnancies was 38.2 weeks (95% CI 37.9 to 38.6).
